table.step: Setup (forms/tiers, capacities, marks, start amounts, limit, initial state, loss tally)
table.ruleA: 6 forms; volume 10,8,12,6,9,7; upper 7,6,9,5,7,5; lower 3,2,4,2,3,2; start 3,6,6,2,2,1; all GREEN; line limit 38; waste 0
table.ruleB: 6 tiers; budget 10,8,12,6,9,7; heat 7,6,9,5,7,5; cool 3,2,4,2,3,2; start 3,6,6,2,2,1; all COLD; stack limit 38; drop 0

table.ruleA: Add the charge-table entry for this cycle to each form; volume not enforced
table.ruleB: Add the ingest-schedule entry for this cycle to each tier; budget not enforced (schedule identical to charge table)

table.ruleA: Sequential in order 1..6; if contents > volume, excess goes to form n+1 (already arrived before n+1 is handled) and form set to volume; form 6 excess to waste; at or below volume nothing
table.ruleB: Sequential in order 1..6; if count > budget, excess to tier n+1 (arrives before it is handled) and tier set to budget; tier 6 excess dropped; at or below budget nothing

table.ruleA: Read after Step 2; GREEN with contents >= upper mark -> HOT; HOT with contents <= lower mark -> GREEN; else unchanged; at most one change per cycle; record (cycle, form, before, after)
table.ruleB: Read after eviction; COLD with count >= heat mark -> HOT; HOT with count <= cool mark -> COLD; else unchanged; at most one change per cycle; log (cycle, tier, before, after)

table.ruleA: Amounts from contents at start of step using post-Step-3 status: GREEN floor(c/4), HOT floor(c/2); all computed first, applied together; each loses its amount; GREEN amount to waste; HOT amount to form n-1, form 1 HOT to waste; volume not enforced
table.ruleB: Amounts from count at start of step using post-step-3 state: COLD floor(c/4), HOT floor(c/2); all computed first, applied at once; each loses its amount; COLD amount dropped; HOT amount to tier n-1, tier 1 HOT dropped; budget not enforced

table.ruleA: Sum all six; if total is MORE THAN 38, every form becomes floor(c/2), removed units to waste, record cycle; if 38 or less nothing
table.ruleB: Sum all six; if total is 38 OR MORE, every tier becomes floor(c/2), removed units dropped, log cycle; if less than 38 nothing
table.difference: Trigger threshold: A uses strict 'total > 38'; B uses 'total >= 38'. At a total of exactly 38, B halves the whole line and A does not. Halving target (all six positions, floor of half, removed units to the loss tally) is otherwise identical.

table.ruleA: (a) end mix 1..6, (b) end status, (c) all status changes, (d) washout cycles, (e) waste tally, (f) balance check
table.ruleB: (a) end counts 1..6, (b) end states, (c) all state changes in order, (d) reset cycles, (e) drop count, (f) balance check showing both sides

result.probeWhy: Route 1 suggested that the only difference is the Step 5 threshold at a total of exactly 38. I searched by script for a probe where the cycle-1 Step 5 total is exactly 38. The probe also makes form/tier 1 overflow in cycle 1 (8+5=13 > 10), so the sequential cascade into position 2 is exercised. The two documents run identically up to that point. In cycle 1, B halves the line (38 >= 38) and A does not (38 is not > 38). From there the runs diverge in quantities, states, changes, halving cycles and loss. The printed tables also trip the boundary: cycle 5 ends at exactly 38, so B halves there and A does not.
result.differingRule: The line-wide halving in Step 5 fires on a total above 38 in A but on a total of 38 or more in B, so a total of exactly 38 halves the line in B but not in A.
result.trust:
The two routes agree. Route 1 found the Step 5 threshold difference by reading the text. Route 2 confirmed it: the totals before halving were 39,28,36,47,38 on the printed tables and 38,... on the probe, and the runs split exactly at a total of 38. On every run, the balance check (start + inputs = end + loss) held.

Scripts used:
- C:\Users\Jaket\AppData\Local\Temp\om\desk-fm\P10\cmp_p10_claude.py, which runs both documents as one routine and switches only the threshold.
- Earlier files sim.py and probe.py in the same folder. Another process was also writing a sim.py into this folder at the same time and overwrote my copy. Its printed-table results matched mine, so I reported only results from my own uniquely named script.

Caveat: the script encodes my reading of the documents, so it is not fully independent of Route 1. The divergence on the printed tables, at a cycle-5 total of exactly 38, is direct evidence on its own.
